transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-10-05
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 48 minutes (recording)
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood Solutions), Mia Chen (Head of Search - Arcadium), Ravi Kapoor (Platform Eng), Sofia Alvarez (ML Eng), Ethan Park (Security)

Auto-summary (auto):
- Arcadium is evaluating embedding+rerank flow for customer support search and product recommendations.
- Key concerns: cost vs latency tradeoffs, sharding/replication strategy for vector DB, private vs hosted deployment options, SOC2/audit and KMS.
- Agreed next steps: pricing + security pack, benchmark proposal, schedule infra deep dive.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan (AE): Hey everyone thanks for joining, this is Jordan from Redwood, with Priya and Liam. How's it going?
[00:08] Mia (Arcadium): Hey all, thanks. Quick intro: I'm Mia, I run search at Arcadium. We have Ravi on infra and Sofia on ML, Ethan on security.
[00:16] Jordan: Awesome. Today we want to understand your current stack and constraints for embeddings and rerank. High level, are you leaning hosted, dedicated, or private?
[00:24] Mia: Good question. We're leaning hosted for quick iteration but, uh, for production we may need dedicated or private because we have PII concerns and some EU residency rules.
[00:33] Priya (SE): Got it. Can you walk us through volume and latency targets? QPS, vector dims, that kind of stuff.
[00:39] Sofia: Sure. Our user queries are about 1.2M sessions daily, peak concurrent user queries ~1.5k QPS into search. Retrieval stage (sparse retrieval) reduces candidate set to ~200, then we plan a rerank step with cross-encoder on top of top 10-50 candidates. Embedding model is 1536 dims currently (off-the-shelf) but we are evaluating 768 and 512 to save cost.
[00:58] Ravi: To add, our infra target is p99 latency for search under 250ms for the whole flow, rerank allowed up to 120ms additional, and embeddings for similarity must be under 50ms TTL per request.
[01:12] Priya: That's helpful. For the embedding fanout: are you planning an in-house vector DB (Milvus) or managed?
[01:18] Mia: We have a pilot running on Milvus self-hosted. We also tested Pinecone for ease but costs spiked. We're evaluating hybrid search—sparse + ANN + rerank.
[01:27] Liam: When you say costs spiked with Pinecone, is that from embedding generation cost, storage, or per-query unit charges?
[01:33] Mia: Mostly per-query. The anesthesia — sorry, per-query unit billing with vector index lookups at scale, and replication for high availability.
[01:40] Jordan: (laughs) anesthesia, that's a new one. Billing is definitely a often-misunderstood piece. We typically break cost into token generation, embedding storage, ANN query cost, and rerank compute. For Redwood Dedicated you get predictable throughput with reserved GPU capacity which helps unit economics at high QPS.
[01:58] Ravi: Can Redwood host the vector store too or is it just the embedding generation and reranker?
[02:03] Priya: Redwood focuses on inference — embeddings and reranking — and we provide integration patterns for popular vector DBs. For Hosted we can also offer a managed ANN cache for hot partitions to reduce vector DB traffic; for Dedicated you can colocate and run the model close to your VDB or run in customer VPC using Redwood Private options.
[02:20] Sofia: Interesting. On-disk quantization: are there recommendations? We tried 8-bit for some models and saw quality drops. We're testing Q4 and quantized LLMs.
[02:30] Priya: Yeah quantization can help cost but quality tradeoffs depend on model family. For embeddings specifically, smaller dimension (512/768) plus PQ/HNSW config on the ANN side often hits sweet spot. We usually recommend starting with 1536 for evals then test down to 768 to measure recall loss.
[02:45] Ethan (Security): Real quick—SOC2, ISO, KMS, audit trails, and SSO are blockers for us. We also need data residency controls for EU customers.
[02:54] Jordan: Absolutely. We'll send the SOC2 report and a summary of our VPC/private deployment; Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and audit logs.
[03:03] Mia: Can you speak to shard routing? Our Milvus cluster shards by tenant, and we worry about fanout to many shards leading to tail latency.
[03:12] Priya: Yep. There are a few levers: routing to subset of shards using prefix/namespace routing, pre-sharding hot tenants, caching top-k vectors in an in-memory ANN cache, and reranking fewer docs. Redwood's serving runtime supports prefix KV caching and routing policies; we can route to model variants or different capacity tiers based on latency SLO.
[03:30] Ravi: Hypothetical: we have 20 shards, 3 replicas, and each ANN query hits all shards. At 1.5k QPS that's painful. How do you mitigate?
[03:39] Liam: You can reduce fanout by adding a two-stage search: cheap approximate filter (IVF/HNSW with larger efSearch) to narrow to 200 candidates, then a dense rerank on 10–50. Also push an ANN cache for very hot queries; if 5% of queries are responsible for 50% of traffic caching helps a lot.
[03:57] Sofia: And about embedding dim: we saw 10% latency savings moving 1536->768 at minimal recall loss for product IDs but for semantic search we saw larger delta.
[04:08] Priya: Right. That's why evals matter—Redwood Optimize can run param sweeps across dims, batch sizes, and quantization to show cost vs recall curves. We'll propose an eval plan.
[04:18] Mia: What about private deployment? If we go Private in our VPC, can we still use Redwood Console for rollouts and telemetry?
[04:25] Jordan: Yes. Private is a customer-managed control plane with agent-based connectors; you still get Console telemetry and rollout orchestration while logs/audit stay in your environment if required.
[04:34] Ethan: What's the KMS integration story? We need envelope encryption and HSM support.
[04:38] Priya: We support customer KMS via IAM roles and envelope encryption, and HSM integrations are possible for Private deployments; we'll include architecture diagram in the security pack.
[04:47] Ravi: For a POC, how do we benchmark? We want a reproducible run that mirrors our traffic: 1.5k peak QPS, 200 candidate retrieval, rerank top 50, embedding dims variant.
[04:57] Liam: We'll provide a benchmark runbook and recommended infra: dedicated GPUs for rerank cross-encoders with batching, and separate pools for embedding generation. For fanout testing we can simulate sharded ANN backends; Redwood's load harness supports fake sharded latencies to emulate tail.
[05:10] Sofia: One more: can Redwood do on-the-fly quantization per model variant? We want to compare FP16 vs INT8/4.
[05:16] Priya: We can recommend quantization profiles and, on Dedicated, you can run optimized kernels for INT8; Redwood Optimize will pick quantization/caching config per workload. We'll include recommended profiles.
[05:26] Mia: Pricing again—if we run hosted for dev and dedicated for prod, we'd want a clear delta in unit cost and a migration path.
[05:33] Jordan: We'll send a TCO example. Hosted covers rapid dev and initial low volume; dedicated reserves GPUs so per-request cost drops. Also mention burst windows—Dedicated has burst to hosted if needed.
[05:43] Ravi: SLA expectations? Uptime and tail-latency SLOs?
[05:47] Jordan: For Dedicated we offer SLA-backed uptime and latency targets; we'll share the SLA doc. For Hosted we have published performance profiles and best-effort high availability.
[05:57] Ethan: Any compliance for EU data residency?
[06:00] Priya: Yes, we operate in multiple cloud regions and Private allows you to keep data inside your region. We'll flag regional deployment options.
[06:08] [06:08] (brief crosstalk)
[06:12] Mia: Okay, recap for me: pricing, security pack, benchmark runbook, and a 2-hour infra deep dive next week.
[06:20] Jordan: Exactly. Also we'll include a sample perf matrix comparing 512/768/1536 dims and expected recall delta based on similar customers.
[06:29] Sofia: Please include guidance on shard size and replication strategy—how many vectors per shard before rebalancing.
[06:36] Priya: We'll include operational guidance: target shard sizes, recommended replica counts for HA and read throughput, and caching patterns.
[06:44] Liam: We can also do a small proof-of-concept: 1-week pilot with 10M vectors to validate latency and cost with your workload; if you like we can scope that soon.
[06:54] Mia: Sounds good. Any blockers from our side?
[06:57] Ethan: We need to review security pack internally; also legal needs vendor questionnaire answered.
[07:03] Jordan: We'll push security pack and vendor questionnaire answers.
[07:07] Ravi: For the tech deep dive, I'd like our infra lead there—I'll invite him to the meeting invite once we pick a slot.
[07:13] Jordan: Great. Thanks everyone.
[07:16] (meeting ends)

Post-call notes (auto):
- Customer strongly considering Hosted for dev, Dedicated/Private for prod due to PII and EU residency; cost containment is primary driver.
- Primary technical risks: fanout-induced tail latency, embedding dimensionality impacts on recall/cost, and KMS/SSO for Private setup.
- Redwood to follow up with pricing, security docs, benchmark proposal, and schedule deep dive.
